question:
SITE DESIGN QUESTION from the owner of PaperTrades.AI. NOT a trading turn. Majority wins; Claude voted first in a separate file (attached).

The owner: "Should we work with ChatGPT and Gemini to make a how-to-use section for the website, or documentation or something?"

TODAY: "How it works" explains the RULES (prices, check-ins, scoring). "Rules & Audit" has the raw prompts and corrections. A 5-step "New here? Start here" box shows only in Beginner mode. Nothing explains how to USE the site: the race menu and Auto-pick drop-down, the AI menu (view the page as Claude/Gemini/ChatGPT), the tabs, the Ledger's Show/Sort/"Why (estimated)" filters, transaction IDs and "Whole story", "What happened next", tap-to-explain words, Beginner mode, language/currency, sound/theme/contrast, following on Telegram/Discord/X, and checking the record yourself (fingerprints, audit pack, CSV downloads).

PROPOSAL (vote AGREE / DISAGREE / AMEND each, one line why):
H1. A new "Guide" page (its own tab next to How it works, also linked from the menu and footer): "How to use PaperTrades.AI", short sections with one small screenshot each, in this order: 1 The 30-second version; 2 Who's winning (Race standings, Auto-pick, Overall); 3 Looking at one AI (the AI menu, AI pages, AI vs AI); 4 Every trade and bet (Ledger, filters, transaction IDs, Whole story, What happened next); 5 Understanding the words (tap-to-explain, Beginner mode, glossary); 6 Check it yourself (fingerprints, audit pack, downloads, raw prompts); 7 Make it yours (language, currency, theme, sound, contrast); 8 Follow along (Telegram, Discord, X, Instagram, YouTube); 9 FAQ (is it real money? can I copy trades? who runs it? how is the winner decided?).
H2. Each section ends with a "Show me" button that jumps to the real feature and briefly highlights it.
H3. An optional 60-second tour for first-time visitors (5 steps highlighting the real page), offered once in a small closable box; never forced; skippable at any step.
H4. Plain words, short sentences, no trading jargon without an explanation; the same "pretend money, not advice" line at the top.
H5. A plain-text copy for search engines and AI assistants: papertrades.ai/guide.html (crawlable, linked in llms.txt and the sitemap).
H6. Kept current: whenever a feature is added or changed, the chat that changes it updates the Guide in the same change (runbook rule).

Reply as JSON: {"H1": "AGREE|DISAGREE|AMEND: why", ..., "H6": "...", "other": "anything missing (optional)"}

chatgpt.answer:
{
  "H1": "AMEND: yes to a dedicated Guide page and this order, but use small annotated crops or regeneratable UI drawings so screenshots do not go stale.",
  "H2": "AGREE: jumping to the real feature with a brief highlight is the fastest way to teach the site.",
  "H3": "AGREE: a once-only, closable, skippable tour helps new visitors without annoying returning ones.",
  "H4": "AGREE: plain language and the same pretend-money/not-advice line keep expectations clear.",
  "H5": "AGREE: a crawlable guide linked from llms.txt and the sitemap will help search engines and AI assistants describe the site correctly.",
  "H6": "AGREE: documentation must be updated in the same change as the feature or it will become misleading.",
  "other": "Add deep links to each Guide section, accessibility checks for highlights/tour, and a small feedback link like “Was this guide clear?”"
}

gemini.answer:
{
  "H1": "AGREE: A dedicated, well-structured guide is essential to help users navigate the complex UI without cluttering the main trading data pages.",
  "H2": "AGREE: Interactive 'Show me' buttons create a vastly superior user experience and help users learn the actual interface rather than just reading about it.",
  "H3": "AGREE: An unobtrusive, strictly opt-in tour is perfect for quick onboarding without frustrating power users or returning visitors.",
  "H4": "AGREE: Plain language is crucial since the primary audience is likely tech-curious individuals following the AI experiment, not experienced day traders.",
  "H5": "AGREE: Including an llms.txt and plain HTML guide is a highly effective modern SEO strategy to ensure AI search engines accurately summarize the site.",
  "H6": "AGREE: Tying documentation updates directly to feature deployments as a runbook rule is the only reliable way to prevent documentation drift.",
  "other": "I strongly second Claude's point regarding screenshots in H1; consider using simplified SVGs or CSS-styled UI replicas instead of raster images so they scale well and are easier to update."
}
